## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

This one-fascicle text is a court Buddhist lecture (*jiǎng* 講) delivered by the otherwise obscure Tang monk [靜居](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9D%9C%E5%B1%85) Jìngjū of the Dà-ān-guó-sì 大安國寺 at the Lín-dé Hall of the Dà-míng-gōng 大明宮 (the imperial palace complex of the late Tang) on the occasion of an unspecified Tang emperor's birthday. The work is set out as a structured doctrinal sermon on the *Huáyán jīng*'s overall structure: the seven places, nine assemblies, 39 chapters across 80 fascicles. Each chapter is briefly summarised, with the cosmic setting, principal interlocutors, and main doctrinal theme. The whole functions as a compact lay-introduction to the *Avataṃsaka*, but addressed to the imperial audience.

**Abstract**

The dating bracket adopted here (859 – 888) is based on the style of the work, the reference to the Líndédiàn 麟德殿 (which functioned as a court lecture-hall in the late Tang, particularly under Yìzōng and Xīzōng), and the institutional setting of the Dàānguósì 大安國寺 — an imperial-foundation monastery active throughout the late Tang and a frequent venue for court Buddhist lectures. No closer dating is internally attested. The text is one of a small number of court-Buddhist *jiǎng* lectures preserved as independent works (most others are referenced only in the *Sòng gāosēng zhuàn* and the *Tang huì yào* 唐會要 without surviving in primary form).

The work's significance is twofold. First, it documents the Tang imperial practice of *huáng-dì jiàng-dàn* 皇帝降誕 ("Emperor's Birth Day") court Buddhist services — a ritual genre attested also in some of [澄觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BE%84%E8%A7%80) Chéngguān's writings — in which Buddhist masters delivered lectures to the assembled court on auspicious imperial occasions. Second, it preserves a compact summary of the doctrinal structure of the *[new (80-fascicle) Huáyán](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010)* from a perspective intermediate between the elaborate Huáyán-school scholasticism (Fǎzàng / Chéngguān) and the lay-philosophical reading of [李通玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%80%9A%E7%8E%84) Lǐ Tōngxuán: a court-pedagogical reading that integrated the basic structural-doctrinal apparatus of the school's mature commentary tradition into an accessible sermon-format. The Taishō text is established on the Korean *Tripiṭaka Koreana* (麗) collated against the *yuán* 原 (original-block) witness.
